title: Hearty Garlicky Egyptian Lentil Stew
description: A garlicky and tender Egyptian dish featuring serrano ham, perfect for a hangover cure, and made shojin-friendly by using vegetable broth instead of animal stock. This stew is packed with flavor and nutrients.
instructions: In a large pot, saute the diced serrano ham over medium heat until crispy, then set aside.
In the same pot, add the chopped onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, until fragrant.
Add the chopped carrots and cook for 5 minutes, until they start to soften.
Add the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, tomato paste, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper to the pot, stirring to combine.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Use an ice bath to shock the stew and stop the cooking process, then let it cool to room temperature.
Reheat the stew over low heat, adding the crispy serrano ham back in, and serve hot.
Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.
Serve with crusty bread or over rice, and enjoy.
